Yaryshiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. On the first day of the German-Romanian occupation of Yaryshiv, about a dozen Jewish men, unaware of the occupiers' intentions, came out to greet the arriving troops and were shot dead on the spot. The town's synagogue, built in 1750, was ruined during the war. Under the subsequent ghetto, hostages were regularly taken to ensure Jews complied with demands to surrender valuables — and were often shot regardless of compliance. Most of Yaryshiv's Jews were murdered near the town in August 1942, and able-bodied workers were deported to the Letychiv labor camp, documented elsewhere in this collection, where most were murdered later that year.
